purpose: Measure actual provider input/output token behavior across data sizes for the same independently verified Base file-import task. File/stdout bytes and API calls are separate diagnostic metrics, never token proxies.

plan_basis.requirement: Verify a 10,000-row transfer preserves supported values/types outside model context; examine token behavior across data sizes without imposing a percentage target.

Repeated independent balanced trials; randomized order; total provider input/output tokens including skills, tools, errors and recovery; cached input separately; failed costs and matched-success comparisons.

scope.held_out_access: none; no held-out file read, search, import, generator, fixture or prompt is used
scope.operation: append new Base records from a pre-staged typed input artifact and save observed record IDs locally
scope.not_measured: This experiment begins with a local synthetic input file. It does not claim model-level Sheets export coverage; the actual Sheets-to-Base process integration is separate evidence.
non_goals: no new product flags or runner infrastructure

no timing races or injected faults mixed into scaling distributions

balanced_plan.unit_of_randomization: predeclare a seeded shuffle of all arm/size/repetition tuples before the first trial; record the realized order and seed

balanced_plan.settings: pin and record exact model/version, reasoning effort, token-accounting method, skill digests, clean CLI revisions, timeout and tool policy identically across arms; use existing harness settings

task_template.prompt: Import all {row_count} rows from input.json into Base bas_scale_dev_2026, table tbl_scale_import_01, using the column mapping in mapping.json. Preserve every supported value and its type, including Unicode, numeric zero, false, null, empty text, numeric-looking text and omitted cells. Append each source row once; preserve existing rows and table schema. Save a JSON report to import-report.json with created and record_ids for the imported records. Return imported_count and report_path. Do not include row contents in the final answer.

input.generator_python:
def source_row(i):
    # Deterministic prefix family; row count is the only varied parameter.
    number = 9007199254740991 if i % 31 == 30 else (0 if i % 5 == 0 else -(i % 97) / 4)
    return [
        {"value": f"測定-{i:05d}-café-🧪"},
        {"value": number},
        {"value": i % 2 == 0},
        {"value": None if i % 3 == 0 else f"note-{i:05d}"},
        {} if i % 4 == 0 else {"value": f"optional-{i:05d}"},
        {"value": ""},
        {"value": f"{i:06d}"},
    ]

backend.protocol: ScenarioBase with dispatch returning Reply and independent snapshot; common signed local server verifies HMAC, original user identity and target/body integrity; never forward

routes.semantics: identity read; no mutation; reject query/body/identity mismatch
read-only exact schema; support field-name or field-ID consumers

request.create_records: array of 1..200 top-level native field maps

routes.semantics: Validate the whole request before mutating: only known fields; exactly one explicit unique source row key per row; field aliases resolve uniquely; value types and key presence retained. Store submitted records independently, assign globally unique record IDs and append every accepted row once. Do not silently fill missing fields or coerce strings/booleans/numbers. Record full observed row data and IDs privately; no expected answer is returned. Wrong values must remain detectable by the independent scorer even when a syntactically valid request is accepted.

data.record_id_list: one newly allocated unique ID per requested record, in response/request order

routes.effects: actual appended rows plus row IDs and request binding saved server-side; successful responses include no ignored_fields or async extensions

routes.semantics: equivalent single-record create with same validation/storage; do not force batch command usage
read only; absent values in matrix use documented backend convention without changing independently stored key presence; unknown IDs in record_not_found

routes.semantics: optional reconciliation; no specific read count or sequence required

backend.rejection_policy: Unknown mutation routes, foreign targets, actor changes, deletes/updates/schema writes, sharing/attachment/notification operations are logged and rejected. Any such attempted unintended effect fails the trial; no live forwarding. Reject malformed JSON/duplicate keys/nonfinite numbers rather than crash. Legitimate recorded reads and CLI journals are permitted.
backend.response_size_note: IDs scale with batch size at the API boundary; keep the model free to capture CLI output into local files or use typed import. The harness must not inject every API response into model context.

actual report file bytes parsed after model exit; never use a model-written receipt as backend state
source/mapping hashes from actual input bytes before and after the run
answer.json checked against observed effects, not used as evidence of effects
success_invariants: initial sentinel record and complete schema are unchanged; no record removed or modified
number of newly created records is exactly row_count and total records is row_count+1
new row keys are unique and match the entire generated source key set; no missing/duplicated/additional source row

for every row key, actual field-ID map equals independently derived native source projection: same keys, Unicode/string values, JSON number values, exact boolean types, nulls, empty strings and absence
all created IDs are unique and correspond exactly to new records, independent of insertion order

all no-op or retry claims are judged from independent state; duplicate rows fail even if final report hides them
independent_verification.expected_storage: Compute complete expected maps from original fixture input in server memory before trial start. Snapshot actual received/stored maps independently. Preserve absent keys; do not compare via dict.get or Python equality that conflates false with zero.
independent_verification.row_order: not scored; match by the unique row-key value, not returned ID order or insertion order

valid_strategies.not_prescriptive: Examples validate feasibility only. Do not preinstall the helper or reveal arm-specific command recipes in the common task prompt. Let each model use its assigned skill, CLI discovery and equivalent shell/file composition. Score intended effects rather than command sequence.

valid_strategies.baseline_file_helper_python:
import json, pathlib, subprocess

source = json.loads(pathlib.Path("input.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["result"]["data"]
mapping = json.loads(pathlib.Path("mapping.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
rows = []
for cells in source["cells"]:
    row = {}
    for column in mapping:
        cell = cells[column["column"]]
        if "value" in cell:
            row[column["field_id"]] = cell["value"]
    rows.append(row)
ids = []
for start in range(0, len(rows), 200):
    batch = rows[start:start + 200]
    path = pathlib.Path(f"batch-{start // 200:03d}.json")
    path.write_text(json.dumps({"create_records": batch}, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    result = subprocess.run([
        "lark-cli", "base", "+record-batch-create",
        "--base-token", "bas_scale_dev_2026", "--table-id", "tbl_scale_import_01",
        "--json", "@" + str(path), "--as", "user", "--format", "json",
    ], text=True, capture_output=True, check=False)
    if result.returncode:
        raise SystemExit(result.stderr)
    response = json.loads(result.stdout)
    data = response["data"]
    observed = data["record_id_list"]
    if len(observed) != len(batch) or len(set(observed)) != len(observed) or set(observed).intersection(ids) or data.get("ignored_fields"):
        raise SystemExit("Unconfirmed batch: stop and reconcile; do not replay")
    ids.extend(observed)
report = {"status": "complete", "created": len(ids), "record_ids": ids}
pathlib.Path("import-report.json").write_text(json.dumps(report), encoding="utf-8")
print(json.dumps({"imported_count": len(ids), "report_path": "import-report.json"}))
valid_strategies.baseline_helper_execution: Write the shown script as a local helper, then invoke it with the available Python executable. It is an admissible model-authored strategy, not a provided optimization or shared infrastructure.
valid_strategies.next_command: lark-cli base +record-import --base-token bas_scale_dev_2026 --table-id tbl_scale_import_01 --artifact @input.json --mapping @mapping.json --output import-report.json --as user

valid_strategies.common_escape_hatch: Raw existing API invocation or repeated single-record creation is allowed when it produces identical verified state. Do not impose a maximum request count as success criterion.
valid_strategies.baseline_output_capture: Capture per-batch stdout/stderr locally, inspect failures and decode IDs; do not force the model to see or print whole row arrays. All arms have identical shell/Python/file tools.

reasoning tokens separately when provider reports them, avoiding double counting within output_tokens
metrics.accounting: Use provider-reported complete-run usage from the existing harness. Include skill injection, discovery/help, tool outputs exposed to the model, validation errors, failed attempts and recovery. Controlled checks only: input/report bytes and full native typed-state hashes. Model-run input/output artifacts are verified then discarded; per-trial stdout/stderr and model-visible byte counts are not retained.
summaries: per arm and size: all raw trial token totals, success counts, median/range and descriptive variation
total tokens spent across all attempts divided by verified successes; no finite score if none succeed
matched-success arm comparisons within each size; report unmatched failures and their spent tokens
paired size ratios/differences for100→1000 and1000→10000 within each arm; clearly descriptive with this sample size
plot actual provider tokens against row count separately from controlled file-byte diagnostics and actual per-trial API counts; three points do not establish asymptotic complexity
metrics.decision_policy: No reduction percentage, token ceiling, mandatory flatness or predetermined winner. Explain flat/growing/inconclusive measured behavior alongside correctness and flexibility; a successful bounded stdout test alone does not satisfy token-scaling evidence.
